items.title: Section: A New Task Opens — Properly Instructing Others, in Eight Kinds

items.zh: 云何教授？當知教授略有八種。
items.en: What is instruction? Instruction should be understood as, in brief, eight kinds.

items.title: Section: Teaching Through One's Own Authority, or Referring a Student to Another — Venerable Upagupta's Example

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，或三摩地為依止故，或於長時共彼住故，於彼慈悲欲為教授。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, either resting on meditative absorption as their support, or through having long dwelt together with someone, wish, out of compassion, to instruct them.

items.zh: 或由其餘諸菩薩眾，或由如來，為作教授。
items.en: Or instruction may instead be given by other bodhisattvas, or by the Tathāgata himself.

items.title: Section: Reading a Student Before Teaching — Disposition, Faculties, Inclination, and Latent Tendency

items.zh: 於教授時，先當審諦尋思其心，如實了知。尋思如實了知心已，尋思其根，如實了知。
items.en: When about to instruct, one should first carefully investigate the student's mind, coming to know it truly. Having truly known the mind, one investigates their faculties, coming to know them truly.

items.zh: 尋思如實了知根已，尋思意樂，如實了知。尋思如實知意樂已，尋思隨眠，如實了知。
items.en: Having truly known the faculties, one investigates their inclination, coming to know it truly. Having truly known the inclination, one investigates their latent tendencies, coming to know them truly.

items.title: Five Gateways of Practice, Matched to Five Dispositions

items.zh: 尋思如實知隨眠已，如其所應，隨其所宜，示現種種所趣入門，令其趣入。謂或修不淨，或復修慈，或修種種緣性緣起，或修界差別，或修阿那波那念。
items.en: Having truly known the latent tendencies, one shows, according to what is fitting and suitable, the various gateways of entry, leading the student in — namely, cultivating impurity, or cultivating loving-kindness, or cultivating the various aspects of dependent origination, or distinguishing the elements, or mindfulness of breathing.

items.zh: 如其所應，隨其所宜，示現種種所趣入門。令趣入已，

items.title: Section: The Middle Way Beyond Eternalism and Nihilism — A Monk's Struggle With Emptiness

items.zh: 為說能治常邊邪執處中之行，為說能治斷邊邪執處中之行。
items.en: One teaches the middle way that counters the erroneous grasping at the extreme of permanence; one teaches the middle way that counters the erroneous grasping at the extreme of annihilation.

items.title: Section: A Cautionary Tale — Mistaking a Meditative State for Liberation

items.zh: 令其除捨未作謂作、未得謂得、未觸謂觸、未證謂證諸增上慢。
items.en: One leads the student to give up the presumption of having done what was not done, attained what was not attained, touched what was not touched, and realised what was not realised.

items.title: Three Underlying Concerns Gather All Eight Kinds of Instruction

items.zh: 如是菩薩八種教授，當知略說三處所攝。云何三處？一、未住心者為令住故，令於所緣無倒係念；二、心已住者為令獲得自義利故，為其宣說正方便道；三、於自所作未究竟者，令捨中間所有留難。
items.en: These eight kinds of instruction should be understood as, in brief, gathered into three underlying concerns. What are the three? First, for one whose mind is not yet settled, causing it to settle, binding attention rightly to its object. Second, for one whose mind is already settled, in order that they attain their own genuine benefit, teaching them the correct means of practice. Third, for one whose own practice remains incomplete, leading them to abandon whatever obstacles still stand in the way.

items.zh: 若知彼心、根、意樂、隨眠已，如其所應，隨其所宜，示現種種所趣入門，令其趣入。當知是名未住心者為令住故，令於所緣無倒係念。若為宣說能治斷、常二邊邪執處中之行。當知是名心已住者為令獲得自義利故，為其宣說正方便道。若令除捨未作謂作，廣說乃至未證謂證諸增上慢。當知是名於自所作未究竟者，令捨中間所有留難。如是三處，當知能攝八種教授。

items.title: Section: Teaching Others Cultivates the Buddha's Remaining Powers — Instruction Concludes

items.zh: 如是菩薩，或由從他得正教授，或由施他無倒教授。能令所餘八力種姓漸得清淨、漸得增長。謂靜慮、解脫、等持、等至智力種姓，諸根勝劣智力種姓，種種勝解智力種姓，種種界智力種姓，遍趣行智力種姓，宿住隨念智力種姓，死生智力種姓，漏盡智力種姓。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, whether receiving correct instruction from another or giving correct instruction to others, thereby gradually purify and gradually strengthen the lineage of the remaining eight powers: the power concerning meditative absorption, liberation, concentration, and attainment; the power concerning the relative strength of faculties; the power concerning the many kinds of resolve; the power concerning the many kinds of disposition; the power concerning where every path of conduct leads; the power of recollecting past abodes; the power concerning death and rebirth; and the power of the extinction of outflows.

items.title: Section: A New Task Opens — Properly Admonishing, in Five Kinds

items.zh: 云何教誡？當知教誡略有五種。一者、遮止有罪現行。二者、開許無罪現行。三者、若有於所遮止、開許法中暫行犯者，如法諫誨。
items.en: What is admonishment? Admonishment should be understood as, in brief, five kinds. First, prohibiting blameworthy conduct. Second, permitting blameless conduct. Third, if someone has, within what is prohibited or permitted, committed a passing violation, correcting them in accordance with the teaching.

items.zh: 四者、若有於彼法中數數輕慢而毀犯者，以無染濁、無有變異、親善意樂如法呵擯，與作憶念。五者、若有於所遮止、開許法中能正行者，慈愛稱歎真實功德，令其歡喜。
items.en: Fourth, if someone violates that same teaching repeatedly and disrespectfully, reproving them in accordance with the teaching, with a mind free of any taint, unwavering, and genuinely well-disposed, and helping them recall the matter clearly. Fifth, if someone conducts themselves rightly within what is prohibited and permitted, lovingly praising their genuine virtue, so that they rejoice.

items.title: Section: Admonishment Concludes, and the Final Point Opens — The Four Means of Embrace

items.zh: 當知是名略說菩薩五種教誡。所謂遮止、開許、諫誨、呵擯、慶慰。
items.en: This should be understood as, in brief, a bodhisattva's five kinds of admonishment: namely, prohibiting, permitting, gentle correction, reproof, and praise.

items.zh: 云何菩薩方便所攝身語意業？當知略說菩薩所有四種攝事，是名方便。如世尊言：菩薩成就四種攝事所攝方便，方名菩薩。
items.en: What are a bodhisattva's skilful deeds of body, speech, and mind? ... It should be understood, in brief, that a bodhisattva's four means of embrace are what is called skilful means here. As the World-Honoured One has said: only a bodhisattva who has accomplished the skilful means comprised by these four means of embrace truly deserves the name bodhisattva.

items.title: Section: Why Exactly Four — Gathering, Taming, and Ripening Every Being Completely

items.zh: 復何因緣，惟四攝事說名方便？謂諸菩薩，略由如是攝事所攝四種方便，於諸有情普能攝受、調伏、成熟。除此無有若過若增。
items.en: For what reason are only these four means of embrace called skilful means? Bodhisattvas, through these four kinds of skilful means comprised by the means of embrace, are able to universally gather in, tame, and ripen beings. Apart from these, there is nothing further, and nothing to add.

items.zh: 何等名為四種方便？一、隨攝方便，二、能攝方便，三、令入方便，四、隨轉方便。

items.title: Section: Drawing Beings In Through Giving First — "Hook Them With Desire, Then Lead Them Into Wisdom"

items.zh: 若諸菩薩先行布施，當知是名隨攝方便。何以故？先以種種財物布施饒益有情，為欲令彼聽受所說，奉教行故。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who first practice giving should be understood as practising the accommodating means of embrace. Why is this? Because first benefiting beings through various kinds of material giving is done in order that they will listen to and accept what is taught, and practice accordingly.

items.title: Section: Kind Speech That Actually Dispels Doubt — The Highest of Three Kinds

items.zh: 若諸菩薩次行愛語，於彼彼處有愚癡者，為欲除彼所有愚癡令無餘故，令其攝受瞻察正理。如是愛語，當知名為能攝方便。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who next practice kind speech, towards those confused about various matters, speak so as to remove their confusion entirely, leading them to grasp and examine the genuine principle involved. Such kind speech should be understood as the capable means of embrace.

items.title: Section: Beneficial Conduct — Actually Guiding Someone From the Unwholesome Into the Wholesome

items.zh: 若諸菩薩知彼有情攝受瞻察正道理已，次行利行，拔彼有情出不善處，於其善處勸導、調伏、安處、建立。如是利行，當知名為令入方便。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, once they know a being has grasped and examined the genuine principle, next practice beneficial conduct, drawing that being out of unwholesome conditions, and, regarding wholesome conditions, encouraging, taming, settling, and establishing them there. Such beneficial conduct should be understood as the entry-inducing means of embrace.

items.title: Section: Shared Work — Practising Alongside, Never Merely Preaching From Above

items.zh: 若諸菩薩如是方便令諸有情得趣入已，最後與其於正事業同共修行，令彼隨轉。由是因緣，令所化者不作是說：汝自無有圓滿淨信、圓滿尸羅、圓滿惠捨、圓滿智慧，何賴於善勸導於他，諫誨、呵擯、與作憶念。是故菩薩所行第四同事攝事，當知是名隨轉方便。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, having in this way led beings to genuinely enter the wholesome path, finally practice the genuine task alongside them, so that the being continues to follow along. Through this, the one being guided is never able to say: you yourself lack complete pure faith, complete discipline, complete generosity, complete wisdom — what standing do you have to well encourage others, to correct, to reprove, to help them remember? For this reason, the fourth means of embrace a bodhisattva practices, shared work, should be understood as the accompanying means of embrace.

items.title: Section: The Entire Chapter's Seven-Fold Teaching Concludes

items.zh: 如是菩薩四種方便，若總若別所攝身業、語業、意業，是名方便所攝三業。於諸有情能正攝受、調伏、成熟。
items.en: In this way, a bodhisattva's four means of skilful embrace, whether taken all together or individually, comprise deeds of body, speech, and mind — this is called the three deeds comprised by skilful means, able to rightly gather in, tame, and ripen beings.

blocks.text: The last part of the bodhisattva's training in fascicle 38: instructing, admonishing, and the four means of embracing others. A short passage (0504b22) is untranslated. Fascicle 38 ends today.

Eight kinds. One instructs "resting on concentration, or having long dwelt with someone, out of compassion"; or has another bodhisattva or the Tathāgata instruct them. Master Cháng Bǎi: if one has taken a disciple but cannot teach them, find someone who can.

"First investigate the student's mind, then faculties, then inclination, then latent tendencies." Then show the fitting gate: impurity, loving-kindness, dependent origination, the elements, or the breath. Teach "the middle way countering eternalism and annihilationism", and help the student "give up the presumption of having attained what was not attained".
To settle an unsettled mind; to free a settled mind; to remove obstacles for one whose work is not done.

Prohibiting the blameworthy; permitting the blameless; gently correcting a passing lapse; reproving a repeat offender "with a mind free of taint, unwavering, well-disposed"; and "lovingly praising genuine virtue, so that they rejoice".

Giving, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and shared purpose: "only a bodhisattva who has these is called skilled in means". Giving first draws beings near. Kind speech "removes confusion entirely". Beneficial conduct "draws beings out of the unwholesome and establishes them in the wholesome". Shared purpose: one practises what one teaches, "so that no one can say: 'You yourself lack this'".
What awakening is, and what the bodhisattva does to reach it: study, teaching, practice, guidance. Fascicle 39 continues the chapter on the lineage of the powers with the perfection of giving.

quiz.q: "Instruction is of eight kinds." What do the five gateways correspond to, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the five purifying objects — Tiantai's five meditations for stilling the mind
quiz.why: "What is instruction? It should be understood that instruction is, in brief, of eight kinds." Master Cháng Bǎi: like the five purifying objects mentioned before — also Tiantai's five meditations for stilling the mind.

quiz.q: Before teaching, "investigate inclination." What examples do the masters give?
options: Miào Jìng: liking to serve as abbot or prior; Cháng Bǎi: loving kitchen duty — conviction in kitchen work
quiz.why: "Having investigated and truly known the faculties, they investigate inclination, truly knowing it." Venerable Miào Jìng: he likes being abbot, likes serving the saṅgha as prior. Master Cháng Bǎi: if a disciple especially likes volunteering in the kitchen, he has conviction about kitchen work.

quiz.q: "Teaching the middle path countering eternalism, and the middle path countering annihilationism." What do the masters say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: contemplating "this ceasing, that ceases" removes clinging to permanence; Miào Jìng: the first is emptiness of self, the second emptiness of phenomena
quiz.why: "They teach the middle path countering eternalist clinging, and the middle path countering annihilationist clinging." Master Cháng Bǎi: contemplating "when this ceases, that ceases," one won't cling to permanence. Venerable Miào Jìng: so the first phrase is contemplation of self's emptiness; the second, of phenomena's emptiness.

quiz.q: "Removing overestimation — 'unattained thought attained.'" Someone thinks the body vanishing means acceptance of non-arising. What is it really, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: merely a sign of access concentration — still an ordinary state
quiz.why: "Causing them to abandon overestimations — thinking done what isn't, attained what isn't, touched what isn't, realised what isn't." Venerable Miào Jìng: it's only a sign of access concentration — still an ordinary person's state.

quiz.q: "Admonishment is of five kinds." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish instruction and admonishment?
options: instruction concerns concentration and wisdom; admonishment concerns precepts
quiz.why: "What is admonishment? It is, in brief, of five kinds: first, prohibiting blameworthy conduct; second, permitting blameless conduct." Master Cháng Bǎi: instruction concerns concentration and wisdom — teaching calm and insight; admonishment concerns the precepts.

quiz.q: For repeat offenders, "rebuke and help them remember." What must one do, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: restate the time, place, event, and words — or the disciple may deny it
quiz.why: "Towards one who repeatedly and contemptuously violates these, with an undefiled, unwavering, friendly intention, rebuking them according to the Dharma and helping them remember." Master Cháng Bǎi: one must restate the circumstances — time, place, event, and words said — otherwise the disciple may not admit it.

quiz.q: "Giving first is the means of drawing in." What saying does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: "first hook them with desire, then lead them into the Buddha's wisdom"
quiz.why: "If bodhisattvas first practice giving, this is called the means of drawing in. Why? First benefiting beings with various gifts, so that they'll listen to what is said and follow the teaching." Master Cháng Bǎi: "First hook them with desire, then lead them into the Buddha's wisdom."
